Let \( a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots \) be the unique sequence of nonnegative integers less than 397 with \( a_0 = 1 \) and

\[ a_{n+1}(a_n + 1)^2 \equiv a_n \pmod{397} \]

for all nonnegative integers \( n \). Given that \( a_{2026} = 9 \), compute the remainder when \( a_0 + a_1 + \cdots + a_{2026} \) is divided by 397.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Work modulo \(397\). First note that no term \(a_n\) is \(0\): if \(a_{n+1}=0\), then the recurrence gives \(a_n\equiv 0\pmod{397}\), and repeating backwards would force \(a_0=0\), contradiction.

Define

\[
b_n \equiv a_n^{-1}\pmod{397}.
\]

Then \(b_0=1\). From

\[
a_{n+1}(a_n+1)^2 \equiv a_n \pmod{397},
\]

divide by \(a_n a_{n+1}\):

\[
\frac{(a_n+1)^2}{a_n} \equiv \frac1{a_{n+1}} \pmod{397}.
\]

But

\[
\frac{(a_n+1)^2}{a_n}
= a_n+2+\frac1{a_n}.
\]

In terms of \(b_n\), this is

\[
b_{n+1} \equiv b_n+2+\frac1{b_n}\pmod{397}.
\]

Hence

\[
a_n=\frac1{b_n}\equiv b_{n+1}-b_n-2 \pmod{397}.
\]

Summing from \(n=0\) to \(2026\),

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv b_{2027}-b_0-2\cdot 2027
\pmod{397}.
\]

Since \(b_0=1\),

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv b_{2027}-1-4054
\equiv b_{2027}-4055
\pmod{397}.
\]

We are given \(a_{2026}=9\), so

\[
b_{2026}\equiv 9^{-1}\pmod{397}.
\]

Then

\[
b_{2027}\equiv b_{2026}+2+\frac1{b_{2026}}
\equiv 9^{-1}+2+9
\equiv \frac{100}{9}\pmod{397}.
\]

Thus

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv \frac{100}{9}-4055
\pmod{397}.
\]

Now \(4055\equiv 85\pmod{397}\), so

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv \frac{100}{9}-85
= \frac{100-765}{9}
= -\frac{665}{9}
\equiv \frac{129}{9}
\pmod{397}.
\]

Finally, \(9\cdot 279=2511\equiv 129\pmod{397}\), so

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n \equiv 279 \pmod{397}.
\]

\[
\boxed{279}
\]
